sanskrit: viśvaṃ vivyajmi pṛthivīva puṣṭam āyadāyat prati gṛhṇāmy annam | vaiśvānarasya mahato mahimnā syonam asmabhyaṃ madhumat kṛṇotu ||
english: I spread out all nourishment as the earth does; whatever food comes to me I receive. By the great majesty of Vaiśvānara (Agni, the universal fire), may he make it sweet and comfortable for us.

sanskrit: triśṛṅgam asi durabhidharṣam indrāya dhriyase | pūṣā te prāśitā ||
english: You are three-horned, hard to assail; you are upheld for Indra. Pūṣan is your first taster.

sanskrit: pāhi no agne tanvaṃ pāhi gāḥ pāhi yat tanūkṛtam | ahutādāv amartyau tāv asmān pāto aṃhasaḥ ||
english: O Agni, protect our body; protect the cattle; protect whatever belongs to the person. Those two immortal ones who are eaters of the unoffered oblation—may they guard us from harm.

sanskrit: yau devānām ahutādāv amartyau svarbhānuś ca svarjyotiś ca | tayos tvāsyena prāśnāmy agneṣ ṭvā vaiśvānarasya tvāsyena prāśnāmi ||
english: Those two immortals among the gods who are eaters of the unoffered—Svarbhānu and Svarjyoti—with their mouth I taste you; I taste you with the mouth of Agni Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: dakṣaś ca tvā mānasaḥ prāśnītāṃ svarbhānuś ca mārutaḥ | mā pṛṇan pūrtyā vi rādhi mo vayaṃ prajayā dhanena ||
english: May Dakṣa the mental one taste you, and Svarbhānu the Marutic one. May the generous one not fail through his bounty; and may we not fail in offspring and wealth.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣyasya te pito anādhṛṣyaśavasaḥ | sarvavīrāḥ sarvātmāno bhakṣaṃ kriyāsma ||
english: O drink (pitu), you who are irresistible, whose strength is irresistible—may we, with all heroes and all selves whole, partake of your substance.

sanskrit: kāmo me rājñi pra viveśa tvāṃ tam ahaṃ nir hvaye punaḥ | gṛheṣu goṣu me mano akṣyor astu me bhago jihvāyām astu me raso bāhvor astu me balam ūrvor astu me javaḥ ||
english: O queen, desire has entered into you; that desire I now call back from you. May my mind dwell in my home and cattle, may my fortune be in my eyes, may the taste be on my tongue, may strength be in my arms, and swiftness in my thighs.

sanskrit: divo 'si nirmathitaḥ pṛthivyā adhy udbhṛtam | samudrād ucyase jātam akṣyāmayabheṣajam asy ātharvaṇam ||
english: You are churned out from the sky, raised up from the earth; you are said to be born from the ocean. You are the Ātharvaṇa remedy for eye disease.

sanskrit: pūṣā parastād ā vartayatu catasro bhūmyā diśaḥ | sagalika puṣalika punar no naṣṭam āyati jīvena bhunajāmahai ||
english: May Pūṣan from beyond turn back the four directions of the earth. O Sagalika, O Puṣalika, may what was lost to us return; with life let us enjoy it.

sanskrit: yad ābharac chṛtad agnis tejane naṣṭavedanam | khargaleva punar dattaṃ punar asmā aśvinā naṣṭam ājatam ||
english: Whatever the blazing fire carried away, scorching it—the knowledge of what was lost—as given back like a khargala, O Aśvins, drive back to him what was lost.

sanskrit: yady asy apriyajā yadi vānyata ābhṛtaḥ | visalpakasya bheṣajīr devīr āpa imā mama ||
english: Whether you were born from something unpleasant, or brought from elsewhere—these divine waters of mine are the remedies of Visalpaka.

sanskrit: yavasya pūtikasya dṛśāmbasyota garmutaḥ | teṣāṃ sam agrabhaṃ śuṣmam āśūnāṃ dhāvatām iva ||
english: Of barley, of the pūtika plant, of the dṛśāmba herb and also of garmutas—I have seized their vital force, like swift ones running.

sanskrit: yas tanuḥ praturvaṇī vadha iva prasarpati | mayūraḥ kila te viṣaṃ kṛkavākuś ca jakṣatu ||
english: The thin creeper that crawls forward like a deadly weapon—the peacock, they say, and the cock shall consume your poison.

sanskrit: udīcīnaḥ pra tanoti nitatnir bhūmyām adhi | ojmānaṃ paśya vīrudho mithunā sam avīvanat ||
english: Stretching northward, the nitatni herb spreads itself over the earth. See how the paired plants have together strengthened the vigor-bestowing one.

sanskrit: ni tvātanaṃ nitatninā pari tvāgāṃ sahīyasā | śyenād abhidravīyasā suparṇān nikarīyasā ||
english: I have stretched you down with the nitatni, I have encompassed you with what is more powerful, with what is faster than an eagle, with what surpasses the suparṇas.

sanskrit: yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ niraṣṭhaviṣam asmṛtam | agniś ca tat savitā ca punar me jaṭhare dhattām ||
english: Whatever here even of honey—poison extracted, forgotten—may Agni and Savitṛ place that back again in my belly.

sanskrit: agne rudrasya jāyāsi duhitāsi prajāpateḥ | uccaiḥśloke dānapatni haviḥśrava upa tvā hvaya upa mā hvayasva | nariṣṭā nāma vā asi ||
english: O fire, you are the wife of Rudra, the daughter of Prajāpati. O mistress of gifts, renowned for oblations, of high fame—I call to you, call back to me. You are indeed named Nariṣṭā.

sanskrit: yathāsau hariṇo vṛṣā kūlād adhi praskandati | evā ni ṣkanda pitryād bhagaṃ jayantī dhanaṃ jayantī ||
english: As that tawny bull leaps down from the bank, so leap down from the paternal share—winning prosperity, winning wealth.

sanskrit: ṛjiśvā mahyam abravīd gandharvasyānuśāsanam | etat te pativedanam ||
english: Ṛjiśvā spoke to me the instruction of the Gandharva: this here is the means of winning a husband for you.

sanskrit: pāṭā bhinattu kumbhaṃ pāṭā kumbhīṃ gadohanīm | pāṭā sarvasya pātrasya vadhūṃ kṛṇotu viśvataḥ ||
english: May the pāṭā plant shatter the pot; may pāṭā shatter the pot used for milking; may pāṭā make her the bride of every vessel from all sides.

sanskrit: apehi takmaṃś cara paro anyam asmad iccha puruṣaṃ kaṃ cid eva | veda te takman pitaraṃ veda mātaram ||
english: Go away, O fever! Move far away from us; seek some other man, whomever it may be. O fever, I know your father, I know your mother.

sanskrit: śamīvān asi śāmīvataḥ śamīvān ābhiśokiḥ | abhiśoko hārṣaṇir harṣaṇo jāñjabhiḥ ||
english: You are associated with the śamī tree, you who are śāmīvata; associated with śamī is the burning one. The burning one is the son of Hārṣaṇi, Harṣaṇa is from jāñjabhi.

sanskrit: yaḥ paśūnāṃ mārjanīyo yaṃ tvam aṃśena bhejiṣe | abhīhi takman gardabhaṃ na mām abhyetum arhasi ||
english: He who is the sweeper of cattle, in whom you share as your portion—go to that donkey, O fever; you have no right to come to me.

sanskrit: visrasā nāma te mātā kiḥkiśo (⟨ kiṣkiṣo?) nāma te pitā | śimidā nāma te svasā ||
english: Visrasā is the name of your mother; Kiṃkiśa (or Kiṣkiṣa?) is the name of your father; Śimidā is the name of your sister.

sanskrit: giriṃ gaccha girijā asi girau te māhiṣo gṛhaḥ | dāsī cakram āsthāya nāmlāte ni krandayiṣyati ||
english: Go to the mountain; you are mountain-born; the buffalo's lair is your home in the mountains. A slave woman mounted on a wheel will make Nāmlāta wail.

sanskrit: ā vāto vātv anaghaḥ sarvasya dūto abhiśastipāḥ | jalāṣam it pra siñcati tad viṣasyāpa siñcatu ||
english: May the sinless wind blow here, the messenger of all, the protector against accusations. It sprinkles the healing jalāṣa—may it wash away that poison.

sanskrit: yām asyati pṛśnibāhur iṣṭaṃ haridruparṇyam | tām asya niṣ khidāmasi yathā jīvāsi bhadrayā ||
english: That desired haridru-leafed plant which the speckle-armed one shoots—we pull it out for him, so that you may live in well-being.

sanskrit: aśrāntasya tvā manasā yunajmi prathamasya ca | utkūlam udvaho bhav- -oduhya prati dhāvatāt ||
english: With the mind of the unwearied and with that of the first one I yoke you. Become one who lifts uphill—having drawn up, run back.

sanskrit: etaṃ dantaṃ nirṛtyā ghoram āhur yasta āsann avarūḍha eṣaḥ | taṃ durhārde pra hiṇomi ghoraṃ sa no mā hiṃsīj jyāyaso mā kanīyasaḥ ||
english: This tooth they call the terrible one of Nirṛti—the one that descended and is now seated in you. That terrible one I send into the hard-hearted; may he not harm us, neither the elder nor the younger.

sanskrit: śivaḥ śagmo bhavatu danta eṣa mā no hiṃsīj jyāyaso mā kanīyasaḥ | aghamāram aghaśaṃsaṃ nirṛthaṃ taṃ te dantaḥ sacatāṃ ghora eṣaḥ ||
english: May this tooth become auspicious and propitious; may it not harm us, neither the elder nor the younger. The evil-slayer, the evil-proclaimer, the useless one—may this terrible tooth of yours accompany him.
